treatments_received.treatment: attendance at AED of Queen Mary Hospital
source: The plaintiff attended the AED of Queen Mary Hospital (“QMH”) on 29 February 2016 with neck and lower back sprain.
He was admitted to orthopaedics unit and was discharged on 3 March 2016.

He underwent physiotherapy and at the follow-up by the orthopaedics out-patient at QMH on 27 May 2016, it was noted that pain had subsided with physiotherapy and analgesics with only complaint of numbness with no neurological signs, no back tenderness and negative SLR test.
The plaintiff was discharged from his physiotherapy sessions on 22 June 2016 but, besides numbness, there were apparently residual back pain, tenderness and deterioration of SLR tests.
He then underwent occupational therapy and on work capacity evaluation on 30 August 2016, he again “self-reported” pain over lower back pain etc.
In the follow-up at QMH orthopaedics clinic on 25 November 2016, it was noted: “pain improved, leg numbness similar, not taking analgesics.”
He then underwent occupational therapy and on work capacity evaluation on 30 August 2016, he again “self-reported” pain over lower back pain etc.
